items.q: What is the definitive and curative management for hepatorenal syndrome (HRS)?
opts: Liver transplantation
Lifelong hemodialysis
Bilateral renal artery stenting
Peritoneovenous shunt placement
items.exp: Liver transplantation is the definitive management for hepatorenal syndrome. (Book p1009)

items.q: What is the recommended dosing and titration schedule for intravenous terlipressin used to reverse splanchnic vasodilation prior to liver transplantation in HRS?
opts: 1 mg IV every 4–6 hours, titrating up to 2 mg IV every 4–6 hours (max 12 mg/day)
2 mg IV stat followed by 1 mg IV every 12 hours (maximum 4 mg/day)
0.5 mg IV continuous infusion doubling every 24 hours (max 6 mg/day)
4 mg IV every 8 hours with rapid taper after 48 hours (max 16 mg/day)
items.exp: Terlipressin is administered as 1 mg IV every 4-6 hours, titrated up to 2 mg IV every 4-6 hours, with a maximum dose of 12 mg/day. (Book p1009)

items.q: Which medical regimens are used to counter splanchnic vasodilation and serve as a pharmacological bridge to liver transplantation in HRS?
opts: Terlipressin, subcutaneous Octreotide plus oral Midodrine, or Norepinephrine
Dopamine infusion, oral furosemide, and intravenous loop diuretics
Nitroprusside, oral hydralazine, and intravenous labetalol
Spironolactone, amiloride, and intravenous hydrochlorothiazide
items.exp: Medical therapy to prevent splanchnic vasodilation until transplant includes: Terlipressin, subcutaneous Octreotide + oral Midodrine (oral alpha agonist), or Norepinephrine. (Book p1009)

items.q: In the medical management of hepatorenal syndrome, midodrine is administered as an ________ and functions pharmacologically as an ________.
opts: Oral agent; alpha-adrenergic agonist
Intravenous infusion; beta-2 agonist
Subcutaneous injection; somatostatin analog
Intramuscular depot; calcium channel blocker
items.exp: Midodrine is an oral alpha-agonist (oral α agonist) used in combination with subcutaneous octreotide. (Book p1009)

items.q: A 49-year-old patient with decompensated cirrhosis and type 1 hepatorenal syndrome (HRS-AKI) is listed for urgent orthotopic liver transplantation. While awaiting donor organ availability, what medical regimen should be instituted immediately to reverse splanchnic vasodilation?
opts: Terlipressin 1 mg IV Q4-6H titrated up to 2 mg Q4-6H (or octreotide plus midodrine)
Aggressive volume resuscitation with 5% dextrose and forced furosemide diuresis
Empirical high-dose oral spironolactone 400 mg daily with potassium chloride
Bilateral renal denervation via catheter-based radiofrequency ablation
items.exp: Medical management to counter splanchnic vasodilation until liver transplant includes terlipressin (1 mg IV Q4-6h up to 2 mg Q4-6h, max 12 mg/d), octreotide plus midodrine, or norepinephrine. (Book p1009)

items.q:
Match each pharmacological agent used in hepatorenal syndrome with its specific administration detail:
1. Terlipressin
2. Midodrine
3. Octreotide
opts: 1: 1 mg IV Q4-6h titrating to 2 mg IV Q4-6h (max 12 mg/d); 2: Oral alpha agonist; 3: Subcutaneous (S/C) administration
1: Subcutaneous administration; 2: 1 mg IV Q4-6h (max 12 mg/d); 3: Oral alpha agonist
1: Oral alpha agonist; 2: Subcutaneous administration; 3: 1 mg IV Q4-6h titrating to 2 mg
1: 1 mg IV Q4-6h; 2: Subcutaneous administration; 3: Oral alpha agonist
items.exp: Terlipressin is given IV 1 mg Q4-6h up to 2 mg Q4-6h (max 12 mg/d); midodrine is an oral alpha agonist; octreotide is given subcutaneously (S/C) in combination with midodrine. (Book p1009)
